items.title: Hentoff Nat — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: My father’s name was Simon Hentoff.

ctx.x: Tell us about your parents: your father’s name, your mother’s name.

My father’s name was Simon Hentoff. He came here from the old country, which was Russia. He didn’t want to be drafted into the Czar’s army, and more to the point, he didn’t want to be the victim of a pogrom. There were some of those then. My mother also came – her name was Lena Katzenburg – from the old country. The story she tells is that one day the word came in the ghetto that the Cossacks were coming. Her own mother popped her into the oven and closed the cover. Fortunately the oven was not lit, or I wouldn’t…
When you say the old country, can you be a little more specific?
